Live: Netanyahu bloc leads with 53 seats after 90% of votes counted, Opposition at 48Israel Election 2026 Live Updates: Israel's Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's bloc is tied with the opposition grouping led by former military chief Gadi Eisenkot, early exit polls showed, pointing to a deadlock in a closely watched election. The election, the first since Hamas' unprecedented October 7, 2023, attack, recorded a turnout of 77.7%, the highest since 1999. For Netanyahu, blamed by opponents for the security failures that preceded the attack and his refusal to set up an independent commission of inquiry, his political future is at stake. Eisenkot's Yashar party is leading an alliance seeking to unseat Netanyahu's Likud party and its right-wing allies. Vote counting is on after a day of strong voter turnout. A party or alliance needs at least 61 seats in parliament to form a majority government. Two leading Arab parties also made strong gains and could emerge as kingmakers. Final results may take days, followed by potentially protracted coalition negotiations as rival blocs scramble to secure a parliamentary majority. The election offered voters a chance to pass judgment on Netanyahu's leadership following wars in Gaza and with Iran, as well as Israel's growing international isolation. Netanyahu, the country's longest-serving prime minister with 19 years in office, has repeatedly survived political crises. But the latest contest could pose another major test of his hold on power.
